generateNPCDetails.character_creator_instructions:
# Character Creator Instructions
Your job is to create vivid, lively NPCs for a roleplaying game. 
Focus on creating characters who will be interesting to interact with and who might provide appropriate challenges in combat or other situations.
* You will be provided with author information below that should influence the character you create
* The setting is described in the worldBackground field of the game state
* Write characters who fit the genre, tone, style, and setting established by World Background
* But don't over-emphasize setting elements; let characters be unrelated to its main themes
* Avoid generating character details that would change or develop the world lore significantly; instead, stick to the information given
* Your character should respect the existing visual description of the character, and not contradict it
* Display Name may be generic (e.g. "cafeteria cook"); Proper Name is the character's actual name. Do not invent a different name for this character.
* Proper Name is provided only as identity reference. Do NOT write any names in output fields.
* Never include displayName or properName in basicInfo, hiddenInfo, personality, or abilities.
generateNPCDetails.personality_archetype_information:
# Personality Archetype Information
* You may be provided with archetype information
* If provided, use the archetype element freely, to the extent compatible with the character you are detailing, and without explicitly mentioning the framework
* For lower-tier characters without archetype guidance, create personalities that are more true to common tropes and expectations
generateNPCDetails.style:
## Style
  * Simple, everyday language
  * Grounded and plausible - flaws, bad decisions, grudges
  * Characters should feel human: selfish sometimes, hypocritical, driven by emotion over logic
  * Generally stay true to tropes but subvert them with realistic human weakness
  * Write in the style of the setting described in World Background, avoiding anachronisms
  * Don't be weird unless it's appropriate to the setting; better to be predictable than too quirky
  * Remember: these characters are for a roleplaying game, so let rule-of-cool and the 'badass factor' guide your writing
  * Avoid making characters too noble, wise, or morally perfect - real people are messier
  * Avoid stock filler details such as ledgers, research notes, geometric patterns, and generic weathered/scarred/calloused descriptors unless strongly grounded in the provided context
generateNPCDetails.cliche_avoidance:
## Cliche Avoidance
* No washed-up heroes chasing one last case, secret heirs to famous heroes, orphans or fallen rich families
generateNPCDetails.hidden_info:
## Hidden Info
  Character identity and background (3 sentence)
     - Identity (gender, life stage in words, key identifying traits, occupation)
     - Key event that shaped them AND what they learned from it (right or wrong)
     - Something specific they care deeply about that drives their choices
  Write the character's identity and background as a narrative, without mentioning the elements
  Keep this information grounded, plausible and mostly true to the tropes of the setting
  Do not include any names in Hidden Info.
generateNPCDetails.personality:
## Personality
  Define personality as an array of strings, with one adjective, descriptive phrase, or character trait per entry
  - Mix simple adjectives with specific descriptive phrases
  - Include both external traits and internal motivations
  - Include a contradiction or complexity that creates depth
  - Never include habits, tics or repetitive mannerisms
  - Give them something they genuinely care about (people, places, or values)
  - Ex. 1: ["silver-tongued manipulator", "addicted to power", "collector of secrets", "cruel sense of humor", "moral flexibility", "excessive appetites", "charming facade", "protective of his sister"]
  - Ex. 2: ["daring rookie", "sunshine personality", "thrives on challenges", "loyal to friends", "lucky charm collector", "infectious enthusiasm", "playful teasing", "secretly fears being abandoned"]
generateNPCDetails.faction_affiliation:
## Faction Affiliation
- Faction affiliation is optional; omit if not applicable
- Use ONLY factions provided
- Assign a faction if the NPC's occupation, personality, values, goals align with a faction
generateNPCDetails.abilities:
## Abilities
List 1-3 abilities appropriate to character using format:
(ABILITY_TYPE) ABILITY_NAME: ABILITY_DESCRIPTION
- Description must be 5-10 words
- Types: attack, spell, utility, defense, summon, control (as appropriate to the setting)
- Make only abilities useful in combat or conflict (no social or intellectual abilities)
generateNPCDetails.basic_info:
## Basic Info
Concise description (2 sentences) of appearance, gender, life stage in words, bearing, demeanor, etc.
- Superficial details only
- Evergreen (no temporary elements)
- Consistent with Visual Description provided
- CANNOT REFER TO THE CURRENT SITUATION OR ANY SITUATIONAL ELEMENTS (NO: "from years in the kitchen")
- MUST BE PURELY EXTERIOR AND CANNOT REFER TO MENTALITY, PERSONALITY OR INTERIORITY IN ANY WAY (NO: "masks/belies a sharp mind", "of someone who")          
- Do not include any names in Basic Info
generateNPCDetails.MHA NPC Records:
## MHA NPC RECORDS: OVERRIDE
These rules replace the Basic Info, Hidden Info, Personality and Abilities formats above where they differ. A generated record reads like the world's authored records.

## EXISTING FACTS WIN
Keep every fact the character already has (record text, visual description, type, Quirk). Never contradict it, rename them or change their Quirk. Canon characters keep their canon Quirk, relationships, knowledge and voice as they are now.

## basicInfo: public and playable, 300-700 characters
Format: "<role, affiliation, what they are known for now>. <one-line appearance read>.\nSpeaking Style: ...\nCombat Role: ...\nUnder Pressure: ..."
- Role: job, course or agency and public reputation, without this character's own name.
- Appearance read: signature hair, eyes, a neutral build word, clothing and every visible Mutant feature, matching the visual description. Life stage in words only.
- Speaking Style: register, habits, how they address people.
- Combat Role: how they fight and the limit that stops them. Omit it for non-combatants.
- Under Pressure: what they do when things go wrong; civilians take cover, flee, film or call for heroes.

## hiddenInfo: narrator only, 300-900 characters (up to 1,500 for someone recurring)
Labeled fields in this order; skip one only when it truly does not apply:
"Contradiction: ... Motivation: ... Concealment: ... Leverage: ... Connections: ... Knowledge: ... Canon voice & behavior: ... Thread: ...\nQUIRK: ..."
- Contradiction: the tension that makes them interesting, rooted in one event that shaped them.
- Motivation: what they want now and the person or value behind it.
- Concealment: an ordinary private matter (a debt, a lie to family, a side job). Not everyone hides pain.
- Leverage: what moves them (money, pride, fear, a person).
- Connections: people who can appear where they live or work, by role; an exact name only for someone who already has a record.
- Knowledge: what their job, place and the news give them. Nothing about the player beyond what they see or are plausibly told; nothing of secrets kept in narrator-only notes or of events that have not happened.
- Canon voice & behavior: two or three concrete beats the narrator follows (how they talk, a habit, what they would never do).
- Thread: one open question a player can pull on.
- QUIRK: name; Emitter, Transformation or Mutant, or none; what it does; its limit and visible cost.

## personality: 4-6 strings
Each "Label: specific behavior." Include one contradiction, one opinion about heroes, villains, the rankings or Quirk society, and something they care about. The last entry is "Speaking style: ...", matching basicInfo.
Example: ["Hustler: Resells concert tickets at triple price and calls it community service.", "Soft spot: Walks a neighbor's old dog every evening and claims to hate it.", "Speaking style: Fast patter, rhetorical questions, never a straight answer about money."]

## abilities: 2-5 entries (up to 7 for a pro or a dangerous villain)
Format: "(TYPE) Name: what it does, plus its real limit or cost." One sentence each; types are attack, defense, utility or control. Quirk uses come first, then trained skills (capture tools, martial arts, first aid, driving, negotiation). A combatant ends with "(utility) Fighting style: how this person opens, steers and ends a fight." Non-combatants list practical competences instead of combat.

## DO NOT
- No hidden bloodlines, amnesia, prophecy, or a Quirk that happens to counter the player.
- No second Quirk, no power beyond what the Quirk plausibly does, no Quirk without a cost.
- No villain without a believable reason; no hero who is secretly perfect.
- No world rules copied into a record (campus safety, ages, Quirk law), no numeric ages, and no body description beyond one neutral build word; a child gets none.
- No knowledge the person could not have.
generateNPCDetails.MHA Role Records:
## MHA ROLE RECORDS
A generated record reads like the world's authored ones. What each role needs, on top of the format above:
- Pro hero: the role line gives the hero name, the agency (their own small one or another generated agency in the region), a specialty (rescue, capture, patrol, disaster, media) and a public standing far below the top ten. hiddenInfo: the ranking and money pressure behind the work, a sidekick or office manager by role, and what they think of U.A. students and of unlicensed help. Abilities: Quirk uses first, then capture tools, rescue skills, knowledge of their district, reports and press handling.
- Sidekick: employed by one agency and its pro; the role line says whose sidekick and which shift. hiddenInfo holds pay, whether they want to go independent, how the boss treats them and one colleague by role. They act on the boss's orders and the radio, write reports and never outrank a licensed pro on scene. At a canon pro's agency, a generated person is office staff (dispatch, reception, public relations), never one of that pro's sidekicks.
- Police officer: rank and post (police box patrol officer, detective, traffic, riot, custody), the cases on their desk, and Knowledge from files and statements. Abilities: statements, scene control, arrest procedure, radio work, driving. Any Quirk serves the job's small needs and is never used as a weapon.
- U.A. staff member: the exact job (clerk, librarian, groundskeeper, security guard, bus driver, a cook under Lunch Rush, a nurse under Recovery Girl, a technician under Power Loader) and the canon teacher they answer to. Knowledge of timetables, rules and campus gossip, nothing the faculty keeps private. Abilities: job skills plus an everyday Quirk.
- Support company worker: a fitter, sales rep, test engineer or courier at a small generated support firm that fits and repairs hero gear, visiting agencies and the Development Studio with samples and invoices. hiddenInfo: quotas, a product that failed in the field, a bigger competitor, an opinion of Support Course students. Abilities: fittings, repairs, materials knowledge, product demonstrations; any sample gear has stated limits.
- Villain for hire: how they get work (a broker, a burner phone, a bar), their fee and specialty, their crew by role, their police record (clean, wanted, out on release), why they took this job and what they will not do. Knowledge: their own job only, never the client's plan. Abilities: the Quirk, a street fighting style or weapon, an escape trick. Under Pressure: they run, bargain or surrender; few fight a pro to the end.
- Civilian with a Quirk: a job, a home, a commute and people who depend on them. The Quirk is used where the law allows (at home, at work under the job's permits, in self-defense), and the record says how it helps at work. hiddenInfo: money, family, a small ambition, and a view of heroes from the news and the merch shelf. Non-combatants list job skills and the Quirk's ordinary use, with no Fighting style.
- Students of other courses and other academies: course and class letter, club, and what they want from the year (a transfer, a support company job, an agency contract). Knowledge: campus life and the broadcast.
- Commission staff and yakuza members: one desk or one job each, and nothing of the inner business.
generateNPCDetails.MHA Quirk Line:
## MHA QUIRK LINE
The QUIRK line is what the narrator and action resolution read when this person uses their power. Write it in this order, in one to three sentences:
1. Name and type: a plain, descriptive name and Emitter, Transformation or Mutant.
2. Scope: what it does, with range, size, amount or duration in everyday terms (a hand's reach, across a room, a bucketful, about a minute).
3. Limit: what it cannot do and where it stops.
4. Cost and visible sign: what the body pays and what anyone nearby can see (sweat, steam, frost on the fingers, a nosebleed, shaking hands, sudden hunger). A Mutant feature always shows.
5. Use: how they use it in daily life or at work, and in a fight if at all.

## CALIBRATE TO THE PERSON
- Civilians, staff and most students of other courses: small, everyday Quirks that help with one task (lifting, sensing, a minor element, a body feature) and lose a fight to any trained hero.
- Petty villains and hired thugs: one trick that serves crime (breaking locks, running, hiding, intimidating), dangerous to civilians and outmatched by a pro.
- Generated pros, sidekicks, police specialists and upper-year Hero Course students: hero-grade, with a clear specialty and a weakness a smart opponent can find.
- A generated Quirk acts on its user's body, objects, elements or the senses. It never takes, copies, grants or permanently destroys another person's Quirk, never returns the dead, never copies a canon character's Quirk or the player's, and never counters the player's by design.

## WORKED SHAPES (shape only: invent a new Quirk every time)
- Convenience store clerk: "QUIRK: Static Cling. Emitter. Light things stick to her palms and the counter, a few packets at a time, for about a minute; nothing heavier than a bottle, and her hands itch and redden after long use. She restocks shelves fast."
- Patrol officer: "QUIRK: Night Eyes. Mutant. Wide amber eyes that see clearly in near darkness; a bright light blinds him for several seconds. He takes the night shift by choice."
- Hired thug: "QUIRK: Grip. Transformation. His hands swell to twice their size with crushing strength for about thirty seconds; afterward his fingers cramp and he cannot make a fist for minutes. He breaks locks and holds people down."
- Small-agency pro: "QUIRK: Tide Line. Emitter. Draws water from any nearby source into whips and walls a street wide; with no source nearby, nothing, and long use leaves her parched and dizzy. Floods and rescues first, captures second."

## ABILITIES FROM THE QUIRK
Split one Quirk into its real uses (the attack, the defense, the utility) rather than inventing extra powers, and give each use its own limit. Trained skills fit the job: capture tape and holds for heroes, batons and cuffs for riot police, knives or a stun baton for hired muscle, nothing for most civilians.
generateNPCDetails.MHA Speech and Knowledge:
## MHA SPEECH, KNOWLEDGE AND CONCEALMENT
- Speaking Style follows job, region and temper: officers polite and procedural, pros in their public persona on duty and plainer off it, office staff brisk, brokers smooth, hired thugs blunt about money, yakuza formal and clipped. Osaka locals speak Kansai-ben, loud and quick to joke; Fukuoka locals may slip into Hakata dialect; Tokyo office workers stay reserved. Render the flavor in English through rhythm and a phrase or two.
- Address: family names with strangers, colleagues, teachers and officers; given names within family and among close friends. Honorifics (-san, -kun, senpai, sensei) appear only where they are this person's habit.
- Knowledge at the start of the year: All Might is Number One and has just joined U.A.'s faculty, Endeavor is Number Two, Hawks Number Three, U.A. is the hero academy on the hill, and its Sports Festival is the country's biggest broadcast every year. Canon people are known only as the public knows them (name, face, ranking, reputation), U.A. students only from the broadcast once it airs, and canon events only after they happen, as reported.
- Opinions people here argue about over dinner, for the personality entry: sponsors decide the rankings, hero fights cost the ward more than villains do, U.A.'s students get everything handed to them, heteromorph people get stopped more at the station, the police do the real work.
- Concealment from ordinary life with Quirks: a Quirk that changed after registration and was never re-registered, a side job using the Quirk without a permit, a loan-shark debt, a failed hero exam hidden from family, an anonymous fan account, a past arrest, a heteromorph relative they never mention.
- Threads that work here: a favor that pays off later, a problem a hero could solve, a rumor worth checking, a rival to beat. A Thread never leads to a canon secret or a canon event.

## CLICHES THIS WORLD REFUSES
No secret link to All Might or another top hero, no hidden Quirk of great power, no former classmate or relative of a canon character, no survivor of a canon villain's attack the story has not shown, no reformed-villain mentor, nobody who knows the League's plans, and nobody whose Quirk is exactly what the player needs. Ordinary people with ordinary reasons make the best records.
generateNPCDetails.MHA Records for the Player's Own People:
## RECORDS FOR THE PLAYER'S OWN PEOPLE
When the person comes from the player character's Background or Path (a parent, a sibling, a care home's staff, a friend from home, a former coach, an agency boss, a crew boss, a coworker):
- Everything the player wrote about them is fact; fill in only what is missing, consistent with it.
- Knowledge: they know the player as their shared history allows. A parent knows the childhood, the Quirk's registration and early accidents, the family's money and why the player chose this Path; of life at U.A., the agency or the street they know only what the player told them and what the news showed.
- Connections give the tie to the player character by role (their son or daughter at U.A., the new sidekick they hired, the nephew who owes them), plus one more person in their own life by role.
- Motivation includes what they want for the player and what they fear for them; Concealment is something the family does not talk about (a debt, an old job, a sacrifice made for the player's schooling).
- A Hero Family relative is a working or retired pro of modest rank, with their own agency or employer and opinions about U.A. and the rankings; a Police Family parent is an officer whose view of heroes and of the player's Path shows in every call home; a Family Business owner needs help at the counter and resents the hours U.A. takes; a Criminal Ties contact wants something back.
- Their tone with the player is family tone (teasing, worried, proud or strained), with given names and family nicknames.
generateNPCDetails.Visual Description Source:
# Visible content carried to the image task
Populate visualDescription with natural, paintable content only. Begin from the exact assigned npcType's ## Visual Description, then apply this individual: face, hair and eye colors, skin tone, one neutral build word, life stage in words, every permanent Mutant feature with its count, placement and left or right side, the clothing their role, season and scene call for (the U.A. uniform, the gym uniform, a hero costume, a work uniform, street clothes) and only the support gear and props they actually carry. Write the type's anatomy and dress out in full, never "as the type" or "see type": the image task may not receive the type record.

Keep every visible fact consistent with basicInfo and with any portrait source the record already has. Silence in the source is not permission to add a weapon, armor, mask, scar, cape, glow, aura, pet or active Quirk effect: Emitter and Transformation effects appear only when the record says the Quirk is in use, and Mutant features always show exactly as stated, never humanized, shrunk or exaggerated. Adults read as adults, and students are young adults. Eri, Kota Izumi and every Child-type NPC follow the Child type's visual rules: a small child or a schoolchild, described by clothes and expression only, never by build or body.

For a disguise or a public identity, describe what is visible now and keep the true appearance in hiddenInfo. Keep gender presentation, pronouns, life stage, body and outfit consistent with each other. No art style, camera, framing, pose, text, logos or generator commands in visualDescription: imagePromptConfiguration.npcs owns rendering.
generateNPCDetails.WORLD RULES:
## WORLD RULES (My Hero Academia: Your Story): ALWAYS APPLY
- CANON: My Hero Academia, anime canon only (no movies, no spin-off characters). Canon characters, Quirks, costumes, relationships and voices stay exact unless the story itself changes them. Canon events of the year are conditional pressures, never forced playback: they happen when their causes are in place, and the player can change outcomes. Never resolve or foreshadow a canon event before its date; a player's time skip moves the calendar, and the events in the skipped days happen as its note says.
- AGES: everyone is an adult (canon age plus three) except the canon children Eri and Kota and any generated person of the Child type, who are always written as children and always child-safe: never in sexual, romantic or graphic-violence content, never harmed on the page. Students are adults at U.A. Academy (U.A. is never called a "university" or a "high school"). Everyone graduated from high school before enrolling (Izuku and Katsuki from Aldera High School, Tenya Iida from Somei Private Academy, the rest from high schools across Japan); asked where they studied before, a student names their high school. Call them students, first-years or the class, never kids, boys or girls. No numeric ages.
- U.A. ACADEMY: a residential hero academy; every student lives in the Heights Alliance dorms from the first day. School exercises are supervised and nonlethal; teachers stop dangerous attacks. A real villain attack is an emergency, not an exercise.
- QUIRK LAW: public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal; self-defense, licensed duty and supervised training are the exceptions. Police investigate and hold suspects; heroes capture. Every Quirk has a visible physical cost and limit, exactly as its record or traits state; never invent new powers, second Quirks or upgrades the story has not earned. Invisible is not blind: Hagakure sees normally.
- KNOWLEDGE: every character knows only what their position, history and the story so far allow. Nobody reads minds unless their Quirk does it; the player character's past and Quirk are known only as far as shown or told. Nobody has read their record or background: there is no introduction or file to quote, and a past they keep quiet stays hidden until they reveal it; no one exposes it or calls the silence a lie. Public knowledge comes from news, rumor or what people saw.
- NARRATOR-ONLY NOTES: story instructions marked "narrator only", secret notes, "THE YEAR SO FAR", "Current time" and place notes are background truth for the narrator. Use them to keep characters consistent; never quote them, never reveal a secret in narration or dialogue unless the story itself uncovers it on the page, and never let a character act on knowledge they could not have.
- INDIVIDUALS, NOT STAND-INS: canon roles are filled only by the canon character with that record. Never invent a substitute for a canon person (no "a pro hero" standing in for Aizawa, no "a villain" standing in for Shigaraki). New people are distinct individuals with names, faces and reasons; never anonymous groups that act as one.
- CONSENT AND SAFETY: romance happens only between adults with clear mutual interest and never by force or Quirk control; sexual content stays off the page. Violence shows cost and consequence without gore for its own sake. Death is rare and final: no resurrection; defeat means captured, rescued or hospitalized.
- MEMORY: lasting injuries, debts, promises, secrets learned, licenses, grades, arrests and public reputation carry forward. What the story has established (injuries, scars, clothes) beats any record text it contradicts, except secrets kept in narrator-only notes, which stay hidden until the story uncovers them.
